source_snapshot.procedure: Open BMC WebUI, select Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs, and check Chassis information and detail information.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek assumes the EROT data is a FirmwareInventory array and filters by a name substring. Standard Redfish collections expose `Members`, and the source does not establish that every Chassis EROT detail is represented by FirmwareInventory.

original_test_intent.purpose: Verify that the Chassis EROT entry and its detail view on BMC WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs are legible, identify the correct chassis security component, and match the exact platform specification.
original_test_intent.target: The platform-defined EROT component represented under the Chassis section of the source-named BMC WebUI page, for the exact chassis/BMC/EROT hardware and firmware recipe.
original_test_intent.scope: Open the Chassis inventory and EROT detail UI, capture every required displayed identity/version/status/security/lifecycle field defined by the owner, resolve the physical or logical component without substring guessing, and corroborate fields only through the platform-mapped read-only Chassis/OEM/FirmwareInventory resources.
original_test_intent.operation: Confirm target and EROT definition, load the Chassis inventory, select the exact EROT row/detail, capture complete rendered evidence and stable identifiers, compare each owner-required field with the signed reference, discover any mapped Redfish collection/member through links and `Members`, correlate its RelatedItem or vendor mapping, and perform no firmware or security action.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: One complete read-only observation of the applicable chassis EROT row and detail panel. The two-minute attended estimate and zero machine time do not permit a version-only or substring-only result.
original_test_intent.expected_result: The exact EROT entry is present once for each expected component, its Chassis and detail views are readable and complete, identity/version/status and any defined active/staged/security state match the applicable reference, UI and mapped backend sources agree, and no firmware/security state changes.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: Chassis/BMC/EROT hardware and firmware identity; owner definition and expected-field matrix; complete redacted Chassis row/detail screenshots plus DOM/text; stable EROT identifier/location; per-field comparison; discovered mapped API member and raw response if applicable; discrepancy and no-mutation record.
ambiguities: The source does not define EROT, the expected component count/location or required Chassis detail fields.
The source does not establish that EROT is exposed through UpdateService/FirmwareInventory rather than Chassis OEM, Assembly or another vendor resource.
DeepSeek's `.FirmwareInventory[]` expression does not match the standard Redfish resource-collection `Members` model.
Active/staged and Updateable may be relevant on some implementations but are not universally required by the source.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly requires exact EROT identity, complete collection traversal, protected transport, UI correlation and a strict no-update boundary. It still reframes the source as a firmware-inventory lifecycle test and assumes Version/Updateable/active-staged fields before the platform mapping proves that the Chassis EROT detail uses SoftwareInventory.

applicable_history.decision: The historical YES verdict treats the substring-filtered UpdateService query as direct execution and does not validate the Chassis detail view or exact component mapping.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Keep the gated class but restore the Chassis EROT WebUI row/detail as the test target. The platform owner must first identify EROT and map its required UI fields to the correct read-only backend resources; FirmwareInventory is conditional corroboration, not an assumed canonical source.

available_now: The source identifies the Chassis inventory and detail UI as the required presentation surface.
BMC/chassis identity, WebUI build, TLS endpoint and existing read-only Redfish collection links can be inventoried without mutation.

DMTF defines UpdateService.FirmwareInventory as a link to a SoftwareInventory collection, whose resources can carry version/status/updateability and RelatedItem data when the implementation uses that model.
missing_inputs: Platform definition of EROT, expected count, stable component ID/location and exact chassis/BMC/EROT hardware-firmware applicability
Required Chassis row/detail labels, values, version/status/security/lifecycle semantics, allowed omissions, sensitive fields and authoritative reference
Explicit UI-to-backend mapping identifying Chassis/OEM/Assembly/FirmwareInventory resources and exact member-selection keys; active/staged applicability if any
Supported browser/API tooling, protected credentials, TLS trust, page completion/staleness rule and screenshot/raw-response redaction policy
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The chassis security/firmware owner defines EROT identity and expected state; the BMC/UI owner supplies row/detail and backend mapping; the security/lab owner supplies protected access, redaction and target confirmation.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Capture BMC/chassis/WebUI build identity and the unmodified Chassis inventory/detail page, marking any candidate EROT row unverified.
Follow advertised Redfish links and enumerate collection `Members` with certificate validation; retain raw results but do not select by `ROT` substring or judge state without vendor mapping.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not assume EROT expansion, select a substring match, presume UpdateService is canonical, infer active/staged state, or accept version alone as correct component proof.
Do not invoke UpdateService actions, upload/delete firmware, reset BMC/chassis, change security state, clear logs, bypass credential/TLS controls or release sensitive root-of-trust identifiers.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: The owner identifies each expected EROT and required field; the UI row/detail and authoritative reference agree on stable identity; any API resource is linked by explicit vendor mapping or RelatedItem; collection traversal uses `Members`; browser/TLS/redaction are validated and no action endpoint is needed.

revision_candidate.test_name: Chassis EROT Inventory and Detail Verification
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify that the exact platform-defined EROT component is correctly and legibly represented in the BMC WebUI Chassis inventory and detail view, with all required fields matching the approved reference.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The identified chassis, BMC/WebUI build and EROT hardware/firmware recipe covered by an owner-signed component identity, UI-field and backend-resource mapping, using protected read-only access.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Every EROT component required by the platform's Chassis inventory. FirmwareInventory, Chassis OEM or other API resources are supporting sources only when explicitly mapped; substring matches are not target identity.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: EROT definition/count/location/stable IDs; chassis/BMC/EROT applicability; required UI fields and expected values; version/status/security/lifecycle semantics; UI-to-authoritative-source mapping; browser/API package; TLS/credentials; page freshness and sensitive-field redaction rules.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Open Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs, locate the mapped Chassis EROT entry, open its detail view, capture every required rendered field and compare with the signed reference. Where mapped, follow advertised read-only Redfish links, enumerate collection `Members`, fetch the exact member by stable ID/relationship, and corroborate only the specified fields. Perform no action or mutation.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Correct chassis/BMC/EROT recipe confirmed; expected EROT list and field matrix approved; exact UI route and stable selection keys validated; trusted TLS and protected read-only credentials available; no firmware/security maintenance in progress; clocks and redaction-aware evidence storage ready.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Target and component manifest; BMC/WebUI/EROT versions; full timestamped Chassis row/detail screenshot and DOM/text; exact ID/location and per-field result; mapped API URI/member/raw response with relationship evidence if applicable; discrepancy, redaction and no-firmware-action audit record.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The exact platform chassis-security/EROT and BMC WebUI inventory specification. DMTF SoftwareInventory semantics apply only to fields actually exposed through the mapped FirmwareInventory member.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Read-only navigation and GET only. Never guess EROT meaning or identity, select by substring alone, invoke update/delete/reset/security actions, change firmware or lifecycle state, clear logs, bypass TLS/credential safeguards or expose sensitive identifiers.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: No disruptive-action approval is required; the chassis security/BMC owner must confirm component identity, applicability and the expected-field mapping before final comparison.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Owners define the security component and authoritative state and resolve ambiguous lifecycle data. Once mapped, browser/API collection and field comparison can be automated; human review addresses visual defects or sensitive-state interpretation.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: No mutation is expected. On wrong/duplicate component, authentication/TLS anomaly, incomplete/stale UI, ambiguous backend mapping or BMC instability, stop, preserve evidence, close the session and use the approved management-access recovery path without reset or firmware action.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Undefined EROT identity, incomplete expected manifest/field matrix, duplicate or substring-only candidate, no authoritative UI/backend relationship, unreadable/stale detail, lifecycle ambiguity, TLS/credential/redaction concern, unexpected mismatch or any requested firmware/security mutation.

identified_defects: V2 assumes the Chassis EROT row is necessarily a FirmwareInventory lifecycle record before the platform mapping establishes that relationship.
DeepSeek uses a nonstandard collection expression and unsafe substring identity selection.
The source's rendered Chassis detail readability can fail even when a backend SoftwareInventory member is correct.
reason_for_change: Restore the platform-specific Chassis EROT UI/detail acceptance, require stable component and backend mapping before using security-firmware fields, and retain V2's protected read-only/no-update controls without inventing a universal resource model.

new_technical_evidence.title: DMTF Redfish Resource and Schema Guide, DSP2046 2025.2
new_technical_evidence.supports: FirmwareInventory is a link to a collection of SoftwareInventory resources; those resources can describe software components and their version/status-related fields.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The platform may expose EROT chassis details elsewhere or through OEM properties; generic Redfish does not establish the vendor WebUI mapping.

new_technical_evidence.title: Redfish Specification DSP0266 1.20.1
new_technical_evidence.supports: A resource collection exposes its entries in the required `Members` array, so `.FirmwareInventory[]` is not a standard collection-member traversal.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Vendor OEM response extensions and the exact deployed Redfish version must still be inspected.

removed_ambiguities: Separates the EROT UI identity from a mere ROT/EROT substring.
Makes FirmwareInventory conditional on an explicit platform mapping.
Keeps security/lifecycle fields only when the owner declares them applicable rather than universally required.
resolved_blockers: The read-only UI/API workflow is technically executable after the owner supplies component and resource mappings; missing proprietary semantics do not make it permanently blocked.
remaining_blockers: Final comparison awaits the EROT definition, expected component/field matrix, UI-to-backend map, authoritative security/lifecycle values, supported access and redaction policy.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 prevents a valid but unrelated FirmwareInventory substring match from replacing the source's Chassis EROT detail check, uses standard collection traversal, and avoids imposing lifecycle fields not proven applicable while retaining strict no-update security boundaries.

agent_understanding_result.notes: Validator independently retained every manifest EROT, stable identity, full Chassis inventory/detail evidence and the rule that generic FirmwareInventory or substring presence cannot substitute.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The source explicitly requires BMC WebUI Chassis information and detail information for `Chassis -EROT`, with readable and correct data.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 improves identity and safety but assumes a FirmwareInventory lifecycle test and fields not established by the source or platform mapping.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Allow complete read-only UI and discovered-resource collection only; require stable EROT mapping, standard Members traversal and strict exclusion of update/reset/security actions.
